title: Finite extension polynomial resource contract
objective: Specify and validate a storage-neutral generated-resource contract for dense univariate polynomials over finite extension fields, including exact Sage semantics, one bulk coordinate boundary, differential oracles, and measured scalar-boundary costs without implementing shared FFI
references: SageMath finite field and polynomial semantics
FLINT fq, fq_nmod, and fq_default APIs

handoff.summary: Defines the strict storage-neutral contract for generated finite-extension FqContext, FqElement, and FqPolynomial resources without inventing a fake foreign resource implementation. Context-dependent elements and polynomials are independently owned self-contained handles whose adapters retain a shared reference-counted context; closing the public context releases only its reference and destruction waits for the last dependent clear. The executable close schedule pins that behavior while documenting the current declaration-schema gap for dependent-owned resources. The contract also pins exact context identity, deterministic modulus metadata, Sage-compatible Unicode letter-leading generator names, low-to-high polynomial and power-basis coordinate ordering, canonical residues, trailing-zero normalization, immutable descriptor-plus-coordinate serialization, and one synchronous bulk construction/export callback. A custom GF(5^3) oracle verifies the nontrivial coordinate table [[1,2,3],[4,0,1],[0,2,0]] and coefficient strings against SageMath and the current FLINT-backed Sage.js field. For a 1,000-coefficient GF(3^2) polynomial, current Sage.js scalar construction and SagePack load each measured about 1,000 ms, while validating the complete 2,000-coordinate table and calling one sentinel callback measured about 5 ms; the benchmark explicitly labels that last number as protocol overhead only, not FFI resource performance.
risks: This lane intentionally specifies but does not implement FqContext, FqElement, or FqPolynomial declarations, generated adapters, public wiring, sanitizer-backed lifecycle execution, or WASM lowering.

The current declaration schema cannot attach an owner to an independently clearable owned resource. Initial generated adapters must therefore use self-contained element and polynomial handles that retain/release a shared context internally; dependent-owned schema support is an optional later compiler refinement with the same public semantics.
Power-basis coordinates are an interchange boundary, not canonical live storage; an integration that retains or exposes the host table would recreate the representation coupling this design avoids.
Word-sized characteristics can use packed unsigned residues, but larger characteristics need a compiler-owned exact-integer coordinate region without changing the contract.

The full pnpm test:native command ran for about 436 seconds and reached test/native-kernel.cjs, then failed an inherited foreign-header cache assertion: it observed packages/flint/include/sagejs/fmpq_matrix_ffi.h where the test expected its temporary override-prefix copy. No claimed source in this contract-only lane was involved, so the focused validation set records the executable contract, benchmark, Pyright, strict baselib, and architecture checks while the shared native-header test is repaired centrally.
next_steps: Generate owned context, element, and polynomial resources whose self-contained dependent handles retain/release the shared context and follow the pinned deterministic close/finalizer schedule.
Implement one bulk power-basis construction/export adapter over FLINT fq_default, selecting fq_nmod or fq storage internally without exposing that choice to public mathematics.
Wire the public GF(p^n)[x] parent to resource-to-resource arithmetic and use bulk export only for explicit coefficients, formatting, and SagePack boundaries.
Add sanitizer-backed context/element/polynomial lifetime schedules and prove a credible WASM lowering before replacing the legacy opaque backend.
